facts.text: The ros_gz_bridge configuration declares /clock with rosgraph_msgs/msg/Clock, bridged GZ_TO_ROS.
The ros_gz_bridge configuration declares /cmd_vel with geometry_msgs/msg/Twist, bridged ROS_TO_GZ.
The ros_gz_bridge configuration declares /odom with nav_msgs/msg/Odometry, bridged GZ_TO_ROS.
The ros_gz_bridge configuration bridges the Gazebo topic /joint_states (gz.msgs.Model) to the ROS 2 topic /joint_states with sensor_msgs/msg/JointState, GZ_TO_ROS.
The gz-sim DiffDrive plugin configures left_wheel_joint and right_wheel_joint, wheel_separation 0.34 m, wheel_radius 0.05 m, the cmd_vel command topic and the odom odometry topic.

The DiffDrive plugin declares max_linear_acceleration 1.0, max_angular_acceleration 2.0, max_linear_velocity 2.0 and max_angular_velocity 2.0 after a comment stating that these are velocity limits preventing simulation instability.
The DiffDrive plugin publishes odometry at 50 Hz and names odom and base_footprint as its frame ids.
AMRController creates a publisher for geometry_msgs/Twist on the absolute /cmd_vel topic with queue size 10.

AMRController.publish_velocity publishes the same Twist at 10 Hz for a caller-computed duration, and stop() publishes one all-zero Twist and sleeps; neither reads a reply or checks that the robot stopped.
move_forward and move_backward compute a duration from the local speed attribute, call publish_velocity and then stop.
The README drives the robot with one geometry_msgs/msg/Twist publication on /cmd_vel.
The README instructs the operator to stop the robot by publishing one Twist with linear.x 0.0 and angular.z 0.0 on /cmd_vel.
The README describes /cmd_vel as a ROS 2 to Gazebo only bridge and says Gazebo never sends velocity commands back to ROS 2.
The JointStatePublisher plugin is declared without a <topic> element, after a comment saying it publishes to the /world/*/model/*/joint_state Gazebo topic.
robot.launch.py includes display.launch.py with use_rsp false.
display.launch.py starts joint_state_publisher_gui without a condition; its comment says the sliders publish to /joint_states and that the node is only for testing.
The LICENSE file is the MIT License.
The robot_description package.xml declares the licence Apache-2.0.
The README says the DiffDrive plugin publishes /odom (nav_msgs/Odometry) with the estimated robot position.
The README says the DiffDrive plugin calculates the robot position by integrating wheel rotations and that /odom contains position x, y, z, orientation and velocity.
AMRController.stop() publishes one default-constructed (all-zero) Twist with its publisher and sleeps.

determinism.notes: Event-driven rosbridge fake with no physics step, diff-drive integration, wall-clock pacing or state-hash replay

gaps: the fake is a ROS-free rosbridge contract stand-in, not a recording of captured traffic: it runs no Gazebo physics, diff-drive plugin, robot model, warehouse world or ROS graph
the /odom pose and twist are placeholder values; the fake echoes the last published twist only as a contract effect and does not integrate motion or claim a trajectory
the /clock sample is a fixed placeholder and does not advance with simulation time
the /joint_states names, positions and velocities are two placeholder wheel-joint entries; the real JointStatePublisher plugin publishes the model's own joint set, which this fake does not reproduce

a live /joint_states read may time out or return GUI slider values: the JointStatePublisher plugin declares no <topic> and its comment names the /world/*/model/*/joint_state Gazebo topic, while the bridge reads the Gazebo topic /joint_states (gazebo.xacro:221-236, ros_gz_bridge.yaml:35-39); robot.launch.py also starts joint_state_publisher_gui through display.launch.py, which publishes slider positions on /joint_states

the linear and angular velocity inputs are operator_required: the clone states only the DiffDrive clamps max_linear_velocity 2.0 and max_angular_velocity 2.0 and no reverse or negative bound; site-limits.example.json is an example overlay, not a source

no stop, pause or reset service or action exists in the pinned clone: the e-stop is a sensed-confirmation stop (SAFE-049, simulated only) that publishes the zero Twist and is achieved only on three consecutive fresh /odom samples whose pose is still within the bound; the thresholds are operator_required (fake placeholders in fixtures/estop-confirmation.json) and the client bounds are fake-scale, so a live deployment sets both, with a consecutive count that spans min_span_ms at the 50 Hz odometry rate, in simulation_deployment['estop_confirmation']

the fake starts driving at a placeholder 0.3 m/s and models the DiffDrive speed limiter as a placeholder ramp of 1.0 m/s^2 and 2.0 rad/s^2 per 0.1 s sample with pose integration and simulated stamps, not Gazebo; amr_menu.py and drive_pattern.py are further /cmd_vel publishers that can move the base after a confirmed stop, which a reset's re-confirmation refuses but nothing prevents
the predicate reads the odometry pose only: the twist fields are filled by the gz-sim DiffDrive plugin outside the clone, and the local gz-sim clone is not the Harmonic version this clone uses
the interactive amr_menu.py client and its 10 Hz publication loop are not started; the fake models only the ROS wire contract
a live run requires the operator's Gazebo Harmonic world, ros_gz_sim, ros_gz_bridge and the upstream launch; none of them is started or validated here

safe_state.description: Simulated only: zero velocity commanded on /cmd_vel and the base sensed still on the bridged /odom pose (position and orientation within the operator's bounds) in three consecutive fresh stamped samples within the confirmation bound. The zero-Twist publication alone proves nothing; another /cmd_vel publisher can move the base again; nothing is claimed beyond the confirmation window.
